message.content:
Fix the custom raw HTML toggle buttons in the Zip Code Checker app at /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code. These need to be replaced with proper Polaris components for Shopify App Store submission.

## Files to fix:
1. app/routes/app.zip-codes.tsx - Has custom toggle buttons using raw `<button>` elements with inline styles
2. app/routes/app.delivery-rules.tsx - Has similar custom toggle buttons

Read both files first. Find the custom toggle button implementations (raw HTML `<button>` elements styled as toggles). Replace them with proper Polaris components.

The best Polaris v13 approach for toggle functionality is to use either:
- `Badge` with `tone` prop for status display (if it's just a visual indicator)
- `Button` with Polaris props for clickable actions
- For an on/off toggle, use Polaris `<Checkbox>` or a `<Button>` with `pressed` prop
- Or use `InlineStack` with `Badge` components that are clickable via wrapping in an action

Look at what the toggles do in context. If they toggle active/inactive status for zip codes or delivery rules, the cleanest Polaris approach is:
- Use a Polaris `Badge` to show status (tone="success" for active, tone="critical" for inactive)
- Make the toggle action available through a `Button` with `variant="plain"` or through the row's action menu

IMPORTANT: 
- Only use Polaris components, never raw HTML
- Read the existing code first to understand what the toggle does
- Keep the same functionality, just use proper Polaris components
- Make sure accessibility is maintained (proper labels, keyboard navigation)

content.text:
Confirmed: `Button.children` is typed as `string | string[]` only. A `Badge` element cannot be a Button child. I need a different approach.

The correct Polaris pattern for a clickable status indicator is to use `Button` with a string label, styled with `tone` to match the active/inactive state. Since `Button variant="plain"` with `tone="success"` or no tone gives the right color cues, the simplest solution is:

- Active state: `Button` with `variant="plain"` `tone="success"` and text `"Active"`
- Inactive state: `Button` with `variant="plain"` and text `"Inactive"` (subdued by default)

This keeps the toggle as a clickable plain button with text that communicates the current state, maintains full accessibility, and uses only Polaris. Alternatively, I can wrap the whole thing in a `Tooltip` and just show a plain `Badge` for display + a separate small `Button` for the action — but a cleaner UX is a single clickable element.

The cleanest approach: use `Button variant="plain"` with text children only (the string "Active" / "Inactive") and `tone` to indicate state.

Both files are clean. Here is a summary of every change made.

---

## What was changed

### `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.zip-codes.tsx`

**Before (lines 562–590):** A raw `<button>` element with `style={{...}}` inline CSS simulating a pill toggle, containing a raw `<span>` as the sliding knob.

**After:** A Polaris `<Button variant="plain" tone={...}>` with a string child ("Active" / "Inactive"), wrapped in a `<Tooltip>` that explains the action on hover.

- `tone="success"` when active (green tinted text), no tone when inactive (subdued default)
- `accessibilityLabel` provides screen-reader text describing the action ("Deactivate zip code" / "Activate zip code")
- `onClick` calls the same `handleToggle` handler — identical backend behavior

### `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.delivery-rules.tsx`

**Before (lines 304–332):** Same raw `<button>`/`<span>` pill toggle pattern in the Actions column.

**After:** Same Polaris `<Button variant="plain" tone={...}>` approach with `<Tooltip>` and `accessibilityLabel`. The "Active"/"Inactive" string label and `tone` prop communicate the current state, and clicking calls the same `handleToggle` handler.

### Why this specific Polaris pattern

- Polaris `Button` v13 restricts `children` to `string | string[]` — wrapping a `Badge` JSX element inside it is a TypeScript error
- `Button variant="plain"` with `tone="success"` renders green text when active, and unstyled subdued text when inactive — a clear visual state indicator
- `Tooltip` provides hover context so users understand clicking will toggle state
- `accessibilityLabel` gives keyboard/screen-reader users a full description of the action
- Zero `any` types, zero raw HTML, zero inline styles
